label: Sonic Pi live-code adapter
summary: Use Sonic Pi for audible code, performance, synthesis, sampling, MIDI, or local OSC while preserving portable source audio and explicit timing intent.

handoffs.label: Develop a playable live-code experiment
handoffs.intent: Turn a bounded musical hypothesis into a small playable Sonic Pi source without treating the live system as the project database.
inputs: A player-facing musical idea and the smallest hypothesis to audition
Song-relative or deliberately portable lossless samples when recordings are used
outputs: A commented Ruby source file with musical intent and declared randomness or timing assumptions
An optional lossless audition recording stored as a new experiment artifact
steps: Describe feel, phrasing, dynamics, and performer relationships before encoding timing coordinates.
Use explicit seeds when repeatability matters and keep sample references portable or documented.
Record the smallest useful audition, inspect it, and retain alternatives only when they answer materially different questions.
verification: Confirm the source parses in the intended Sonic Pi version and referenced samples exist.
Listen to the complete experiment and record what the prototype preserves, changes, and leaves unresolved.

handoffs.label: Record a lossless Sonic Pi stem
handoffs.intent: Capture a bounded Sonic Pi performance as a new lossless experiment artifact while keeping the editable source and the listening decision separate.
inputs: A reviewed Sonic Pi source buffer or saved set
A bounded recording duration and destination under the song workspace
outputs: The exact source, app version, take duration, and technical inspection notes
steps: Open the source in the intended Sonic Pi version and confirm the output device before running it.
Use Sonic Pi's Record control for the smallest useful audition; stop the performance before importing the stem into another mix.
Keep the source and recorded bytes unchanged, then hand the new file to EPRS analysis and review.
verification: Confirm the WAV exists, has the intended sample rate/channel layout, and is not silent or clipped.
Compare the recorded duration with the intended musical bars; inspect for accidental GUI tails or duplicated saves.
Record a complete listen and a keep/change/stop decision before promotion.

handoffs.label: Sync with MIDI or Ableton Link
handoffs.intent: Use external timing or audio peers as an explicit performance experiment without making hardware or network state part of the portable source of truth.
inputs: A named MIDI clock/device or an intentionally enabled Ableton Link peer
A musical reason for external timing or live audio exchange
outputs: An editable source with the external dependency named
A lossless captured result plus the device/peer and sync settings
steps: Enable only the intended device or Link peer in Sonic Pi's IO controls; do not assume a connected device is authorized or musically useful.
For v5 MIDI clock, use `use_bpm :midi` with an explicit `quantum:` when bar alignment matters; for Link audio, name the peer and channel in the source.
Record the resulting performance locally and preserve a standalone EPRS stem so the project remains portable if the device or peer disappears.
verification: Confirm the intended MIDI source or Link peer is the one being followed and that the first bar lands where expected.
Check for jitter, phase drift, monitoring bleed, and accidental remote/network exposure.
Treat the result as a performance capture, not a deterministic render, unless all external state is frozen and documented.

handoffs.label: Capture a Sonic Pi session video
handoffs.intent: Use Sonic Pi v5's built-in session recording or GUI streaming for a live artifact or visual experiment while keeping the EPRS release picture path separate.
inputs: A deliberate live-performance or behind-the-scenes brief
A separate approved audio/master path if the capture will become a release candidate
outputs: A session capture with its Sonic Pi source and app version
A review note distinguishing performance documentation from release picture
steps: Use session recording for an intentional live artifact; do not silently substitute it for the frame-accurate EPRS picture renderer.
If using Syphon/Spout streaming, keep the receiver local and explicitly configured.
For a release, rebuild the final picture through the approved EPRS master and picture-review path.
verification: Confirm the capture contains the intended window and master mix, with no private desktop or source-domain information visible.
Watch the complete capture and record whether it is documentation, experiment, or release candidate.

handoffs.label: Drive local visual cues from a performance
handoffs.intent: Send declared local OSC cues to an explicitly configured visual session without creating remote-control authority.
inputs: A local-only OSC address/port chosen by the operator
A versioned mapping from musical events to visual cues
outputs: A preserved cue mapping and editable live-code source
An optional renderer-neutral picture capture reviewed separately from the performance
steps: Confirm both applications are intentionally configured for local OSC before sending anything.
Keep cue names musical and stable while application-specific addresses stay in the adapter source.
Capture any resulting finished film through eprs picture rather than treating the live session as reproducible evidence.
verification: Confirm OSC remains local, expected cues arrive, and no unrequested control surface is enabled.
Verify the finished picture begins at master time zero and record a complete picture review.

preserve: Original recordings outside live buffers, commented musical intent, declared seeds, and any unique playable source
The distinction between performed timing and an authored grid or live-code interpretation
avoid: Embedding irreplaceable audio only inside a live session, silently copying an artist's surface style, or inventing a fixed tempo where none was intended
Opening network control beyond the declared local OSC relationship or implying that a live render is approved
